extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of Indian classical arts; artists and writers interested in applying rasa aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative dimensions from classical Indian rasa theory used to create or judge artistic works (theatre, dance, music, poetry, sculpture). Focuses on how emotional 'flavors' (rasas) are produced, expressed, and received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal of art: produce rasa / transport the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the Natya Shastra, entertainment is a desired effect of performance arts but not the primary goal. The primary goal is to transport the audience into another, parallel reality full of wonder and bliss, where they experience the essence of their consciousness and reflect on spiritual and moral questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art should aim to evoke an aesthetic relish (rasa) that transfigures ordinary emotion into aesthetic delight; success is measured by the audience's transported, reflective experience rather than mere amusement or external recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rasa sutra: rasa produced from vibhava, anubhava, vyabhicaribhava
rubrics_metrics.description: Rasa is produced from a combination of Determinants (vibhava), Consequents (anubhava) and Transitory States (vyabhicaribhava). — (Natyashastra 6.109)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or evaluating a work, examine how causes (vibhavas), manifested effects (anubhavas) and passing states (vyabhicaribhavas) combine to yield the dominant rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vibhavas (Determinants): alambana and uddipana
rubrics_metrics.description: Vibhavas means Karana or cause: it is of two kinds - Alambana, the personal or human object and substratum, and Uddipana, the excitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and develop the situational/person-based causes (alambana) and the stimuli (uddipana) that will reliably elicit the intended rasa in the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anubhavas (Consequents / effects of emotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anubhava, as the name signifies, means the ensuants or effects of emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the outward manifestations and consequences of internal states (anubhavas) so the audience can recognize and taste the resultant rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vyabhicaribhavas / Sanchari Bhavas (transitory/ancillary states)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanchari Bhavas are those passing feelings which are ancillary to a mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transient subsidiary feelings to color and support the dominant emotion without displacing it; these fleeting states enrich and nuance the primary rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sthayibhavas (stable/emotive cores)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Natyashastra lists eight Sthayibhavas with eight corresponding rasas: Rati (Love), Hasya (Mirth), Soka (Sorrow), Krodha (Anger), Utsaha (Energy), Bhaya (Terror), Jugupsa (Disgust), Vismaya (Astonishment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lasting, dominant emotional state (sthayi) is the core from which a rasa is tasted; ensure the work establishes and sustains an appropriate sthayi to anchor the rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sattvika bhavas (psychophysical expressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Natyashastra outlines eight anubhavas or sattvika bhavas: Stambha (Stupefaction), Sveda (Sweating), Romancha (Feeling thrilled), Svarabheda (Break in voice), Vepathu (Trembling), Vaivaranya (Pallor), Ashru (Tears), Pralaya (Swoon or death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic psychophysical signs (sattvika bhavas) are indicators of genuine internal emotion; artists should portray these where appropriate to convince the spectator of the authenticity of feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abhinaya (modes of expression) — gestures, facial expression, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Rasas are created through various means; one way is through the actors' gestures and facial expressions. Expressing Rasa in classical Indian dance form is referred to as Rasa-abhinaya.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate or craft performance technique (gesture, facial expression, body language) so that physical expression reliably communicates the determinants, consequents and transitory states that yield rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic technique: what is stated and how it is stated
rubrics_metrics.description: In the theories of Indian poetics, ancient scholars state that a literary composition's effectiveness depends on what is stated and how it is stated (words, grammar, rhythm), which creates its rasa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For poets and writers, both content and form (diction, syntax, meter, rhythm) must be arranged to produce the desired aesthetic flavor; attention to linguistic devices that arouse and sustain emotion is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sahṛdaya (aesthetic sensitivity of the spectator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sahṛdaya-s are those spectators who 'have been exposed to appreciation of literary work and who have made it a habit to think about the literary work' — because of this previous exposure, they attuned their minds to create the reflection of poetic emotions in their minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rasa presupposes a receptive, cultivated spectator; creators should consider the audience's aesthetic sensitivity and prior exposure when aiming for particular rasas, and critics should recognize the role of sahṛdayatā in reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success criteria for performance (Abhinavagupta)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Abhinavagupta, the success of an artistic performance is measured ... only when it is performed with skilled precision, devoted faith and pure concentration, so that the artist gets the audience emotionally absorbed into the art and immerses the spectator with the pure joy of a rasa experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate performances by technical skill, concentrated devotion, and the degree to which the audience is emotionally absorbed and experiences the intended rasa — not by external awards or reviews alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated Rasas / Navarasa (target emotional flavours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bharata Muni enunciated the eight rasas: Śṛṅgāra (Romance/Love), Hāsyam (Laughter/Mirth), Raudram (Fury), Kāruṇyam (Compassion), Bībhatsam (Disgust), Bhayānakam (Horror), Vīram (Heroism), Adbhutam (Wonder). Later authors added Śāntam (Peace/Tranquility) to make the Navarasa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works may be crafted to aim at one dominant rasa (or a primary/secondary combination); each rasa carries cultural associations (e.g., presiding deity, colour) that inform staging, music, and imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rasa attributes: presiding deity, colour, and pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Nātyasāstra, each rasa has a presiding deity and a specific colour. There are 4 pairs of rasas. For instance, Hāsya arises out of Sringara. (The text lists deity and colour associations for each rasa.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing visual, ceremonial, or symbolic elements of a work (costume, lighting, color palette, iconography), align them with rasa-specific attributes to reinforce the intended emotional flavour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music/raga selection should serve rasa
rubrics_metrics.description: In Indian classical music, each raga is an inspired creation for a specific mood, where the musician or ensemble creates the rasa in the listener. Predominantly all ragas and musical performances in Hindu traditions aim at one of six rasas, wherein music creates 'love, compassion, peace, heroism, comic or the feeling of wonder'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical mode, melodic material and performance practice should be chosen to evoke the intended rasa; in evaluation, judge whether the raga and musical treatment successfully produce the targeted emotional flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sculpture/architecture and formal design to evoke rasa
rubrics_metrics.description: In the theories on sculpture and architecture (Shilpa Shastras), the rasa theories, in part, drive the forms, shapes, arrangements and expressions of images and structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how formal design choices (shape, posture, composition, spatial arrangement) embody and communicate a rasa; three-dimensional art should be read for the moods it sets up in the spectator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rasa as transformative psychophysical/spiritual effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commentators emphasize the psychophysical dimension of rasa, arguing that theatrical and musical art can have a very real influence on psychophysical and even spiritual states, producing a transformative effect on the spectator's organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a work aspires to and achieves psychophysical or spiritual transformation (beyond mere emotion), and whether the methods used (sound, movement, ritual) convincingly produce such effects.
